name: observe
description: A two-service application (obslab: W3C trace context, spans, Prometheus-format histograms, JSON logs with trace IDs) behind a router whose connection tracking serves as flow records: a baseline, then a slow dependency, a lossy network, an error burst with head vs tail sampling, a dropped port and a refused port — what metrics, logs, traces, host counters and flow records each show.

nodes.name: router
setup: iptables -A FORWARD -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT && ip tuntap add dev pl-ab mode tun && ip tuntap add dev pl-ba mode tun && ip link set pl-ab up && ip link set pl-ba up && sysctl -qw net.ipv4.conf.pl-ab.rp_filter=0 net.ipv4.conf.pl-ba.rp_filter=0 && ip rule add iif eth0 table 100 && ip route add default dev pl-ab table 100 && ip rule add iif eth1 table 101 && ip route add default dev pl-ba table 101

checks.name: baseline first: 1000 requests through frontend → backend, all 200; the three signals agree, and every span has its parent
run: for f in ${EVIDENCE}/spans-*.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/log-*.jsonl; do : > $f; done; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl; ${BIN}/obslab load -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/ -n 1000 -c 20 -spans ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ; ${BIN}/obslab spans -slowest 1 ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-backend.jsonl; ip netns exec nl-observe-client ${BIN}/obslab metrics -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/metrics
expect_contains: 4000 spans in 1000 traces, 0 with an error, 0 spans whose parent is missing

checks.name: the backend delays 10 % of requests by 300 ms: the client's p99 jumps; the slowest traces put all of it in the backend span
run: for f in ${EVIDENCE}/spans-*.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/log-*.jsonl; do : > $f; done; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl; ip netns exec nl-observe-client ${BIN}/obslab metrics -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/metrics -save ${EVIDENCE}/m-slow-before.txt >/dev/null; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend curl -s --noproxy '*' 'http://198.18.222.10:8081/admin/faults?slow=0.1&delay=300ms'; ${BIN}/obslab load -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/ -n 1000 -c 20 -spans ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ; ${BIN}/obslab spans -slowest 3 ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-backend.jsonl

checks.name: the same incident in metrics — counters only grow, so take the increase over the incident window: the histogram's p99 (interpolated inside the 250–500 ms bucket) overstates the spans' true p99, and the mean (~30 ms) describes no actual request
run: ip netns exec nl-observe-client ${BIN}/obslab metrics -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/metrics -since ${EVIDENCE}/m-slow-before.txt; ip netns exec nl-observe-client ${BIN}/obslab metrics -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/metrics ; echo 'true percentiles of the frontend server spans:'; ${BIN}/obslab spans -slowest 0 ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl | grep 'frontend server'

checks.name: logs and traces join on the trace ID: the slowest trace's ID finds its log line in both services
run: id=$(${BIN}/obslab spans -slowest 1 ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-backend.jsonl | grep -o 'trace [0-9a-f]*' | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f2); echo "slowest trace: $id"; grep -h "$id" ${EVIDENCE}/log-frontend.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/log-backend.jsonl

checks.name: now the backend is fast but the frontend↔backend path loses 5 % (and adds 5 ms each way): the time sits between the frontend's client span and the backend's server span — the network
run: for f in ${EVIDENCE}/spans-*.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/log-*.jsonl; do : > $f; done; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend curl -s --noproxy '*' 'http://198.18.222.10:8081/admin/faults?slow=0'; ip netns exec nl-observe-router ${BIN}/pathlab set delay=5ms loss=0.05 >/dev/null; ip netns exec nl-observe-frontend nstat -n; ${BIN}/obslab load -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/ -n 1000 -c 20 -spans ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ; ${BIN}/obslab spans -slowest 3 ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-backend.jsonl; echo "frontend host counters: $(ip netns exec nl-observe-frontend nstat TcpRetransSegs TcpExtTCPTimeouts TcpExtTCPLossProbes | tail -n +2 | awk '{printf "%s %s  ", $1, $2}')"; ip netns exec nl-observe-router ${BIN}/pathlab set delay=0 loss=0 >/dev/null

checks.name: the backend fails 2 % of requests with 503: metrics count them at both services; with every trace kept, a tail-sampling rule (errors, or ≥ 250 ms) would keep only those traces
run: for f in ${EVIDENCE}/spans-*.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/log-*.jsonl; do : > $f; done; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl; ip netns exec nl-observe-client ${BIN}/obslab metrics -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/metrics -save ${EVIDENCE}/m-err-fe.txt >/dev/null; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend ${BIN}/obslab metrics -url http://198.18.222.10:8081/metrics -save ${EVIDENCE}/m-err-be.txt >/dev/null; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend curl -s --noproxy '*' 'http://198.18.222.10:8081/admin/faults?fail=0.02'; ${BIN}/obslab load -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/ -n 2000 -c 20 -spans ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ; ${BIN}/obslab spans -slowest 0 -tail-slow 250ms ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-backend.jsonl; ip netns exec nl-observe-client ${BIN}/obslab metrics -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/metrics -since ${EVIDENCE}/m-err-fe.txt; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend ${BIN}/obslab metrics -url http://198.18.222.10:8081/metrics -since ${EVIDENCE}/m-err-be.txt

checks.name: the same at 10 % head sampling (decided before anyone knew the outcome): only the sampled tenth of requests have traces, so only their errors can be found — while the logs still hold every 503
run: for f in ${EVIDENCE}/spans-*.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/log-*.jsonl; do : > $f; done; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl; ${BIN}/obslab load -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/ -n 2000 -c 20 -spans ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl -sample 0.1; ${BIN}/obslab spans -slowest 0 ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-backend.jsonl; echo "frontend log: $(grep -c . ${EVIDENCE}/log-frontend.jsonl) requests, $(grep -c '"status":503' ${EVIDENCE}/log-frontend.jsonl) of them 503; traces kept: $(grep -c '"kind":"server"' ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl)"; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend curl -s --noproxy '*' 'http://198.18.222.10:8081/admin/faults?fail=0'

checks.name: the backend's host firewall DROPs its port: every request ends in a 504 after the frontend's 1 s timeout; the traces have no backend span; the backend logged nothing; Go's error text says 'awaiting headers' whether it was still dialing or waiting for a reply
run: for f in ${EVIDENCE}/spans-*.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/log-*.jsonl; do : > $f; done; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 8081 -j DROP; ip netns exec nl-observe-router conntrack -F 2>/dev/null; ${BIN}/obslab load -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/ -n 40 -c 20 -spans ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ; ${BIN}/obslab spans -slowest 1 ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-backend.jsonl; echo "backend log lines: $(grep -c . ${EVIDENCE}/log-backend.jsonl)"; ${BIN}/obslab logs ${EVIDENCE}/log-frontend.jsonl

checks.name: the router's connection tracking as flow records: the new connection attempts passed through (1 packet, 60 bytes) and nothing came back; the pooled connections still say 'two-way' — flow counters cover a flow's whole life, so they cannot say when it stopped working
run: conntrack -L -o extended -p tcp --dport 8081 2>/dev/null | ${BIN}/obslab flows | awk 'NR==1 || (/SYN_SENT/ && s++<3) || (/ESTABLISHED/ && e++<3)'; echo "flows to :8081 with no reply: $(conntrack -L -p tcp --dport 8081 2>/dev/null | grep -c UNREPLIED)"; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 8081 -j DROP

checks.name: the same port REJECTed with a TCP reset instead: 502 within milliseconds, error 'connection refused' — the error text and the timing name the failure
run: for f in ${EVIDENCE}/spans-*.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/log-*.jsonl; do : > $f; done; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 8081 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset; ${BIN}/obslab load -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/ -n 40 -c 20 -spans ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ; ${BIN}/obslab logs ${EVIDENCE}/log-frontend.jsonl; ip netns exec nl-observe-backend iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 8081 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset

checks.name: repaired: back to all 200 — verify the fix with the same measurement that showed the failure
run: for f in ${EVIDENCE}/spans-*.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/log-*.jsonl; do : > $f; done; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl; ${BIN}/obslab load -url http://198.18.220.20:8080/ -n 200 -c 20 -spans ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ; ${BIN}/obslab spans -slowest 0 ${EVIDENCE}/spans-load.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-frontend.jsonl ${EVIDENCE}/spans-backend.jsonl
